science.qualification: Photosphere color from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum, dimmed toward the limb by the quadratic law Claret (2017), A&A 600, A30 computes from PHOENIX model atmospheres for the TESS band at 3,207 K and log g 4.92 (u1 0.155, u2 0.475): a model, because no fit of this star's limb is used. The disc is unresolved: no map or absolute brightness is implied. Self-luminous, so no lighting.

science.label: Sector 44
science.description: Brightness of the star's surface that reproduces its light as it turns once in 1.9 days, fitted with starry to the TESS mission's own 2-minute light curve of sector 44 (its PDC-MAP flux) (the light varies by 2.2%; the map's curve leaves a scatter of 0.34%, the light's own noise being 0.24%). A light curve fixes how bright each longitude is, not the latitude of what darkens it. In this sector the method of Holcomb et al. (2022, ApJ 936, 138) finds a period of 1.93 d from the autocorrelation, whose peaks have a height of 0.52, a width of 0.47 and a fit of 1.00, and in all 3 of the star's sectors together a period of 1.90 d from the autocorrelation, whose peaks have a height of 0.52, a width of 0.47 and a fit of 1.00; its criteria accept that as the star's rotation. No tilt of this star's axis is known: the map is made at 60°, the middle tilt of axes that point at random. Gaia DR3 lists 6 other stars within 63 arcseconds, with 9.8% of their light and the star's together. A reduction made in this project, not a published map.
science.title: TESS · brightness map made here · Sector 44

science.label: Color + brightness
science.description: The star's color (#ffcd83, its Color dataset) over the brightness map this project made from the star's light in TESS sector 71 (October and November 2023): the map's scale, 97% to 103% of the mean surface, runs from a darker, richer tone of the same hue to the color itself. The contrast is drawn far stronger than it is, so the parts can be told apart: the darkest part gives 5.4% less light than the brightest. Longitudes are fixed by the light curve; latitudes and shapes are not. No color change of the spots is drawn: none is measured. A reduction made in this project, not a published map.
science.title: TESS · the star in its color over its brightness map · October and November 2023
